This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Sri.Manjunatha caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
On 15.10.2023 at about 7.15 p.m., Manjunatha was riding his TVS Jupiter Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-44-V-0419 from Kunigal side towards his native village Chikkasathigere of Mayasandra Hobli, Turuvekere Taluk, Tumkur District.

While Manjunatha was travelling near Thattekere Gate after Yadiur Bridge on NH-75 road,
Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District, at that time the Hyundai Creta Car bearing Reg,No.KA-13-Z-0299 came from Kunigal side towards Hassan was driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the above said scooter from backs side.

Due to impact, Manjunath fell down on the left side of Shantha vs Sunganalli Veerappa Shashidhar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157397169/
2 the road and sustained severe injuries.

Immediately after the accident, Manjunatha was shifted to AC Giri Hospital, B.G. Nagar, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District by the public in a hired vehicle by paying Rs.2,000/-, but the doctors of said hospital confirmed the death of Manjunatha.

sentences.text: After conducting postmortem dead body of Manjunatha was handed over to the petitioners and their relatives, they have shifted the dead body to their native place in a hired vehicle by paying Rs.2,000/- and performed funeral and obsequies ceremony by spending Rs.2,50,000/-.

3. Deceased Manjunatha was aged about 45 years at the time of his death, during his lifetime he was doing agriculture along with Gare work, bar bending and centering work and earning Rs.1,000/- to Rs.1,200/- per day and maintained the family.

Due to death of deceased, the 1 st petitioner, who is the wife, has lost her loving husband at her young age, 2nd and 3rd petitioners are minor children have lost their loving father at their tender age and 4 th petitioner, who is the mother of deceased has lost her loving son.
Hence, all the petitioners are suffering from mental shock, which cannot be compensated by any means and they have lost their earning member and suffered lot to lead their life.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Hyundai Creta Car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299.The
Amruthur police have registered the case against the driver of above said car in Cr.No.159/2023 for the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The above said vehicle having insurance policy with 2nd respondent and it was in force on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

Accordingly, the petitioners have prayed to award compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- from the respondents.
4.
After service of summons, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before this Tribunal and filed separate written statement.
5. The Respondent No.1 in his written statement has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

This respondent has denied the date and time of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the Hyundai Creta Car bearing Reg.No.KA-44-V-0419 by its driver, death of deceased due to injuries sustained in the alleged accident, amount spent by the petitioners, age, occupation and income of the deceased.
The 1st respondent has contended that, the petitioners have colluded with the Amruthur police and registered the case against the driver of offending vehicle.
Further contended that, the offending vehicle has been insured with the 2 nd respondent and it was valid as on the date of accident.
The driver of the said vehicle having valid D.L. at the time of accident.

If any compensation is awarded,
the 2nd respondent has to pay the same.
Hence, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. The Respondent No.2 in its written statement has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law on on facts.

It has admitted the issuance of policy with respect to Car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299 and contended that, the liability to indemnify the owner is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, provision of MV Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of Car, valid R.C., F.C. and confirmation of Sec.64VB of Insurance Act.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.

It is contended that, the car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z- 0299 was no way responsible for the accident and as per crime records the Shantha vs Sunganalli Veerappa Shashidhar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157397169/

entire negligence is on the part of the deceased.
The jurisdictional police have filed false charge sheet against the insured vehicle by colluding with the petitioners.

Further contended that, the driver of above said car was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and thereby the 1st respondent has committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
This respondent has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased, amount spent by the petitioners.

It is the contention of the 2 nd respondent that, at the time of accident, the deceased was riding the scooter without wearing prescribed ISI marked helmet by violating the mandatory provisions of law and hence sustained injuries.
The deceased having no valid driving licence to drive the scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-44-V-0419, which is clear case of "Volunti non fit injuria".
Further contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., the owner and insurer of the above said scooter.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues has been framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Manjunatha?
2.

Whether the petitioner proves that, on 15.10.2023 at about 7.15 p.m., the deceased Sri. Manjunatha died in a road traffic accident that occurred near Thattekere gate after Yadiyur Bridge on NH 75 road, within the jurisdiction of Amruthur police station, Kunigal taluk, Tumkur district due to negligence on the part of driver of the Hundai Creta Car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so,from which respondent?
4. What Order or Award?

11. ISSUE No.1:- In order to prove that, the petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased Manjunatha,
PW.1 has produced Aadhaar card of deceased at Ex.P.5, Aadhaar cards of petitioner No.1 at Ex.P.6,
petitioner No.2 at Ex.P.7, petitioner No.3 at Ex.P.8 and petitioner No.4 at Ex.P.14.

From these documents it is clear that the father name of deceased is shows as Huchappa, petitioner No.1 is wife,
Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of deceased Manjunatha and the husband name of petitioner No.4 is shows as Huchappa, who is the father of deceased.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 to 4 are considered as dependents on the income of deceased and they are considered as legal heirs of deceased.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. ISSUE No.2:-

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 15.10.2023 at about 7.15 p.m., deceased Manjunatha was proceeding by riding his Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-44-V-0419 near Thattekere gate after Yadiyur bridge on NH-75 road, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District, at that time the driver of Hyundai Creta Car bearing Reg,No.KA-13-Z-0299 came from Kunigal side towards Hassan in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the above said scooter from behind.
Due to impact, Manjunatha has sustained severe injuries and succumbed to fatal injuries on the way of hospital.
In support of their contention, the 1 st petitioner examined herself as P.W.1.
P.W.1 has filed affidavit by way of examination-in-chief and reiterated the petition averments.

To prove the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299, P.W.1 has produced documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4, Ex.P.10 to Ex.P.13.
13.
The petitioners have also examined one witness namely Ravikumar K.J. as P.W.2 and he has filed affidavit evidence in lieu of examination in chief.

P.W.2 has deposed that, on 15.10.2023 at about 7.15 p.m., while the deceased Manjunatha was proceeding on the left side of the road on NH- 75, Bengaluru-Mangalore road, near Thattekere village by wearing helmet, at the time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299 driven the vehicle in a rash and negligently manner with high speed and dashed the scooter from back side.
At that time he was proceeding on his bike from 200 meters behind the above said scooter.
Further deposed that, they shifted the deceased Manjunath to the A.C. Giri hospital and when they reached the gate he was succumbed to injuries.
Further P.W.2 has deposed that, after confirming the death of Manjunath, he was informed to the relatives of deceased and lodged the complaint before Amruthur police.
During the course of cross-examination he has denied the suggestion as to the negligence of the deceased Manjunatha.
14. On the other hand, it is the contention of 1st respondent that, the petitioners have colluded with the police and registered the case against the driver of offending vehicle.

The specific contention of the 2nd respondent is that, the car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299 was no way responsible for the accident and as per crime records the entire negligence is on the part of the deceased.
The jurisdictional police have filed false charge sheet against the insured vehicle by colluding with the petitioners.
In support of their contentions, the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299 has not been examined by the respondents.
The respondents have neither examined any witness and nor produced any documents to believe their contention.
Hence, the contention of respondents holds no water.

It is relevant to rely on the decision reported in 2008 ACJ 3981 (SC), in the case of Sudhir Kumar Rana V/s Surinder Singh and others.

sentences.text: Wherein it was held that, 'mere non-possessing of DL cannot be held to be guilty of contributory negligence'.
To put it differently, if a person drives a vehicle without a license, he commits an offence.
The same by itself may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.

From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of complaint from one Ravikumar as per Ex.P.2, Amruthur police have registered the case as per Ex.P.1 i.e., FIR in Crime No.159/2023 against the Hyundai Car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299 for the offenses punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC.

The respondents No.2 contended that, the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased on the ground that the deceased had ridden the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner in a wrong road and dashed to the offending vehicle on left side of the road.
Therefore there is a contributory negligence and same has to be taken into consideration and also argued that there is no U- turn to cross the road and U-turn is 300 meters after the accident plaice.

The petitioner has pleaded that the driver of Hyundai Creta Car bearing Reg,No.KA-13-Z-0299 came from Kunigal side towards Hassan in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the above said scooter from behind.
Therefore there is a sole negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

It clearly shows that, the deceased was riding the motor cycle on wrong side and accident occurred by hitting to the front portion of the both vehicles.
17. The EX.P.11 rough sketch reveals that the accident occurred on road from Bangalore to Mangalore way.

Despite such width, the deceased was shown to have taken the motorcycle to the extreme right edge of the opposite lane, which was meant for one-way traffic in the opposite direction and it is a clear traffic violation.
The rider is bound to maintain his proper lane and exercise extra caution on a curved road.
By failing to do so, the deceased exposed him to a higher degree of risk and contributed to the unfortunate occurrence.

18. When once statutory violations such as wrong-side entry are established, the burden shifts upon the petitioners to rebut the presumption of contributory negligence by showing that despite such lapses the deceased had exercised due care and that the accident was caused solely by the rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle.
19. On the other hand, the defence raised by the respondents that the accident was a result of the self- negligence of the motorcyclist is also not fully borne out by the record.

Except for bare Shantha vs Sunganalli Veerappa Shashidhar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157397169/

sentences.text: In the absence of such material, this Tribunal is drawing an adverse inference against the respondents.
The charge-sheet filed by the Investigating Officer has attributed negligence solely to the driver of the offending vehicle.
Though such a charge-sheet is not conclusive proof, it is a contemporaneous public document carrying substantial weight.
20. Therefore, on a careful consideration of the entire record, this Tribunal finds that both the deceased and the offending vehicle driver were negligent.
In the present case, the offending vehicle is a Creta Car, and the deceased was travelling on a motorcycle.

The evidence on record, particularly the spot sketch and contemporaneous police documents, demonstrates that the accident occurred when the motorcycle, ridden by the deceased, entered the extreme right side of the road in the opposite one-way direction.
At the same time, the offending Creta car, which was in charge of a heavy vehicle, failed to exercise due care and caution.
21. Having regard to the manner in which the accident occurred, this Tribunal is of the considered view that both the deceased and the driver of the offending Creta car were negligent.

Therefore,
while the Creta car driver's rash and negligent driving was the dominant and proximate cause of the accident, the deceased's contributory acts to entering the wrong side of the road cannot be ignored.
On a comparative assessment of negligence, this Tribunal holds that liability shall be apportioned in the ratio of 90% against the driver of the offending vehicle and 10% against the deceased rider.
The liability for payment of compensation shall accordingly follow this apportionment.

Accordingly,
Issue No.2 is answered in the partly affirmative.
22. ISSUE No.3:

As already discussed in Issue No.1 and 2, Petitioner No.1 to 4 are the dependents of the deceased Manjunatha and they are entitled for compensation.
23. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:-
According to petitioners, the deceased Manjunatha was aged about 45 years at the time of his death.
PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of deceased at Ex.P.5 and it shows that, the date of birth of deceased Manjunatha is 03.01.1978.
The accident was occurred on 15.10.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 45 years 9 months.
Hence age of the deceased is considered as 46 years

As per the principles laid down by their Lordships in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation), the multiplier applicable to the present case is '13'.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
30. In this case, respondent No.1 is the RC owner of offending Hyundai Creta Car bearing Reg.No.KA-13-Z-0299 and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer.
31. In view of my finding in issue No.1, the driver of the offending vehicle has contributed 90% for the cause of the accident and deceased has contributed 10% for the cause of the accident.
The petitioners are entitled for only 90% of compensation amount, from the respondents.
The total compensation amount is Rs.25,68,000/- and the 10% amount in the total amount is to be deducted i.e., Rs.2,56,800/-.
Therefore 90% compensation amount comes to Rs.23,11,200/-.

Therefore under these circumstances and above reasons the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners on account of death of deceased in the accident.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Hyundai Creta Car is liable to pay compensation of Rs.23,11,200/- with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioners from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 in the 'Partly affirmative'.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
To put it differently, if a person drives a vehicle without a license, he commits an offence.
The same by itself may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.
The rider is bound to maintain his proper lane and exercise extra caution on a curved road.
By failing to do so, the deceased exposed him to a higher degree of risk and contributed to the unfortunate occurrence.
Except for bare Shantha vs Sunganalli Veerappa Shashidhar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157397169/
6 assertions, the respondents have not placed any documentary evidence to substantiate that the offending vehicle driver exercised due care and caution.
In the absence of such material, this Tribunal is drawing an adverse inference against the respondents.
The charge-sheet filed by the Investigating Officer has attributed negligence solely to the driver of the offending vehicle.
Though such a charge-sheet is not conclusive proof, it is a contemporaneous public document carrying substantial weight.
20. Therefore, on a careful consideration of the entire record, this Tribunal finds that both the deceased and the offending vehicle driver were negligent.
In the present case, the offending vehicle is a Creta Car, and the deceased was travelling on a motorcycle.
The evidence on record, particularly the spot sketch and contemporaneous police documents, demonstrates that the accident occurred when the motorcycle, ridden by the deceased, entered the extreme right side of the road in the opposite one-way direction.
At the same time, the offending Creta car, which was in charge of a heavy vehicle, failed to exercise due care and caution.
21. Having regard to the manner in which the accident occurred, this Tribunal is of the considered view that both the deceased and the driver of the offending Creta car were negligent.
Therefore,
while the Creta car driver's rash and negligent driving was the dominant and proximate cause of the accident, the deceased's contributory acts to entering the wrong side of the road cannot be ignored.
On a comparative assessment of negligence, this Tribunal holds that liability shall be apportioned in the ratio of 90% against the driver of the offending vehicle and 10% against the deceased rider.
